item.title: Anthropic's Compute Costs Outpace Revenue Growth in Q3
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Anthropic is still grappling with the economics of compute
Anthropic disclosed worsening compute margins in its latest IPO filing, revealing rising costs are outpacing revenue growth. The company reported $17 billion in revenue for Q3, up from $11.5 billion in the prior quarter, but operating losses expanded due to soaring compute expenses. Compute costs accounted for 58% of revenue in Q3, up from 48% in the previous quarter, with the company spending $10 billion on compute, including $5 billion under short-term contracts at higher rates. Anthropic relies on neocloud providers like SpaceX, Nscale, Akamai, and Volta for flexible but expensive compute, as its own Direct project cannot keep pace with demand. The company expects compute and infrastructure costs to remain its largest expense as multi-year commitments expand. While strong revenue growth masks the issue, risks like bond market volatility or local opposition could disrupt the compute supply chain, leaving AI labs vulnerable to price fluctuations. The filing highlights the industry’s heavy reliance on trillion-dollar infrastructure buildouts and the fragility of that dependency.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Phone users can detect hidden cameras with flashlight and infrared checks
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: How to use your phone to find hidden cameras
Phone users can detect hidden cameras using flashlight and infrared checks. A 2024 CNN report found Airbnb processed 35,000 support tickets related to surveillance devices in a decade. Airbnb bans indoor recording devices but allows outdoor security cameras. Visitors often distrust short-term rentals, as cameras can be disguised as common items. To check, use a flashlight to scan for lens glints or LED lights in areas like mirrors, smoke detectors, or televisions. Night-vision cameras emit infrared light, detectable via phone camera as purple or white dots. Wi-Fi scanning apps like Fing can identify unfamiliar devices named 'cam' or 'camera,' though some devices may appear as printers or TVs. Bluetooth scans may also reveal cameras. If found, photograph the device, contact police, and notify the platform. Airbnb and Vrbo prohibit indoor cameras, with Airbnb removing hosts and refunding guests in reported cases. Vrbo advises immediate reporting and potential refunds. Methods are not foolproof, as some cameras use local storage, but combining physical and digital checks offers the best chance of detection.

item.title: CrowdStrike Acquires Two AI Security Startups for $500M
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: CrowdStrike to shell out nearly $500M for 2 AI security startups as the market for securing agents takes off
CrowdStrike is acquiring Fiddler AI and Dreadnode for approximately $400 million and $95 million respectively. The purchases aim to enhance CrowdStrike's capabilities in monitoring and securing AI agents and models. Fiddler AI provides observability tools for AI agents, while Dreadnode automates security testing for AI systems. The deals come as companies rapidly adopt AI, straining existing cybersecurity measures. CrowdStrike's Falcon Observe will integrate Fiddler's tools to evaluate agents before deployment, and Dreadnode's testing results will inform Falcon Guardian's security policies. Fiddler, founded in 2018, has raised $99 million, while Dreadnode, founded in 2023, has raised $14 million. The acquisitions expand CrowdStrike's offerings in a growing market where traditional security tools are deemed insufficient for AI-related risks.

item.title: Binance Hack Traced to North Korean Cyberattack Using Fake Job Interviews
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch, PCMag, Engadget, The Verge
Binance confirmed a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft by North Korean hackers using a multi-month social engineering scheme. The FBI attributed the attack to a North Korean unit called 'TraderTraitor,' which exploited fake job interviews and an internal AI tool to infiltrate Binance’s systems. The breach, detected in October, began in June when a Wallet DevOps engineer downloaded a tampered Homebrew package manager via a malicious Google ad. Despite replacing the engineer’s device, the hackers obtained colleague details. In September, attackers impersonated a 'Project Director' to conduct a fake interview, tricking a software engineer into downloading malware disguised as a coding assignment. The malicious file replaced a legitimate development tool, evading detection. By October 20, hackers used the compromised engineer’s access to Binance’s AI tool to control systems, executing a script to steal cryptocurrency on October 29. Binance suspended withdrawals, citing the threat from North Korea, which has been accused of funding its nuclear program through crypto thefts. The exchange rebuilt systems, decommissioned credentials, and enhanced security with AI tools. While 98% of stolen tokens were recovered, the attack highlights vulnerabilities in job interview-based attacks and internal tool risks. FBI and blockchain investigators confirmed North Korea’s involvement, noting the country’s history of targeting crypto firms. Binance reported facing at least 57 suspected North Korean attacks.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: VirusTotal helps detect malicious files and links online
item.description:
Source: PCWorld Original headline: Not sure if a file is malicious? Upload it to VirusTotal
VirusTotal is a web tool used by cybersecurity professionals to scan files and links for malware. Users can paste URLs or upload suspicious files to check them against multiple antivirus engines, receiving up to 10+ threat assessments. The service acts as an additional layer of protection but is not a substitute for traditional antivirus software. It allows detection of malicious activity without requiring file downloads, as Windows may access metadata to trigger payloads. Experts recommend using VirusTotal as a first defense for uncertain files but emphasize that antivirus software remains essential for ongoing protection. The tool helps mitigate risks from phishing, drive-by downloads, and browser vulnerabilities by identifying threats before they execute.

item.title: EU to Build Undersea Cable to Greenland, Bypassing US
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: EU reveals plans for undersea cable straight to Greenland — and could bypass the US entirely to connect up the world
The European Union is advancing an undersea cable project to connect Greenland directly with Europe, bypassing U.S. territory. The Pan-Arctic Cable could eventually link Europe, Greenland, Canada, Japan, and South Korea, with the EU committing $119 million to Greenland’s secure communications infrastructure and the project. The initiative aims to reduce reliance on vulnerable maritime corridors, such as the Red Sea and Baltic Sea, which face security risks like attacks and anchor dragging incidents. The EU also plans an Arctic Cable Hub to monitor and protect subsea infrastructure. Elisabeth Braw of the Atlantic Council noted the project reflects growing European interest in alternative routes due to security concerns and shifting geopolitical dynamics. Challenges include high construction costs, icebreaker support, and complex repairs in Arctic conditions. Previous attempts like Arctic Connect failed, but the Pan-Arctic route avoids that corridor. The plan also depends on Canadian cooperation for its Asian extension.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M for AI-driven cybersecurity funds
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Ted Schlein’s Ballistic Ventures seeks $490M for new funds amid AI-driven cybersecurity boom
Ballistic Ventures, the cybersecurity venture capital firm co-founded by Ted Schlein, is seeking $490 million across two new funds, according to SEC filings. The firm plans to raise $360 million for its third flagship fund and $130 million for Ballistic Ventures Fund B, with no sales recorded at the time of filing. The fundraising follows increased AI adoption, which has heightened cyber threats but also created opportunities for cybersecurity startups. Ballistic Ventures, founded in 2021, has backed companies like Talon Cyber Security and Pangea, acquired by Palo Alto Networks and CrowdStrike respectively. Its ties to Kleiner Perkins distinguish it from rivals, though its investment strategy mirrors that of firms like Forgepoint Capital. U.S. cybersecurity startups raised $11.5 billion in 2025, with AI-enabled companies accounting for 72% of deals through May 2025, per JPMorgan Chase. Microsoft’s Digital Defense Report warns hackers are using AI for phishing, social engineering, and malware development. Ballistic Ventures declined to comment on its fundraising plans.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: How to Check App Permissions on Your Phone
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Your phone's apps could have more permissions than they need – here's how to check
Apps on smartphones may request unnecessary permissions, such as access to location, camera, or messages. Both Android and iOS provide tools to review and manage these permissions. On iOS, users can adjust settings to restrict background location access, limit microphone use, or set location access to 'Allow While Using App.' The App Privacy Report shows which apps accessed data and sensors. Android users can check permissions via Settings > Apps > Permissions, with options to revoke access or set access types like 'Allow Only While Using App.' Both systems require apps to request permissions upon installation, and app stores list requested data. Users can also monitor network activity and adjust settings for specific apps like Google Maps or Uber. Regularly reviewing permissions helps protect personal data from unauthorized access.

item.title: Ancient Egyptian Religious Complex Unearthed via Satellite Imaging
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Satellite Imagery Reveals a 2,600 Year-Old Complex Buried Beneath an Ancient City in Egypt
Egyptian researchers uncovered a 2,600-year-old religious complex beneath Buto using satellite radar and electrical resistivity tomography. The structure, located in the Nile Delta, measures 420 feet long and 203 feet wide, with a mudbrick wall buried 10 to 20 feet deep. Excavations revealed amulets of Egyptian deities, including Wadjet, and a small offering basin, suggesting the site may have functioned as a temple, priestly residence, or funerary structure. The complex dates to the late eighth century BCE or the Saite period (7th–6th centuries BCE). Buto, a former religious and political center of Lower Egypt, was abandoned for 1,500 years before being resettled during the Third Intermediate Period. The discovery highlights the challenges of excavating buried layers beneath clay and silt, with further research needed to determine the site’s exact purpose. Published in Acta Geophysica, the findings offer new insights into Buto’s role during its period of renewed activity.

item.title: Netflix Launches AI 'Discover' Tab for Personalized Content Suggestions
item.description:
Source: Engadget, TechCrunch, Digital Trends Original headline: Netflix Introduces AI-Powered 'Discover' Tab to Help Users Find New Content
Netflix is rolling out an AI-driven recommendation tool called 'AI Discover' to help users find content more efficiently by reducing endless scrolling. The feature, available to a select group of U.S. users on supported TVs in English, introduces a new tab with a red gem icon in the top navigation bar. Users can explore curated themes based on mood, viewing habits, or time constraints, such as 'family movie night,' 'scare me,' or 'quick watches.' These themes narrow content suggestions without relying on traditional genre presets. Once a theme is selected, the AI generates tailored recommendations, with options to refine choices or reset using 'Something Different.' A 'Tune Your Recommendations' button allows users to save preferred titles or block specific content. Netflix described the tab as a 'test kitchen' for experimenting with new discovery methods, with user feedback guiding potential permanent features. The tool is initially limited to English and TV apps, excluding kids profiles, and plans to expand availability soon. The company emphasized AI Discover as part of its ongoing effort to enhance content discovery through real-time personalization.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Apple AirPods require accessories or upgrades for small ears
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Here's how to adjust Apple AirPods for small ears
Adjusting Apple AirPods for small ears requires external accessories or upgrading to AirPods Pro. The AirPods 5 lack ear tips, making a secure fit difficult for users with smaller ear canals. Third-party hooks from KeyBudz and AhaStyle cost $10–$15 to improve retention. AirPods Pro offer multiple ear tip sizes (XXS to L) for better sealing, with silicone or foam options. Users should test fit by trying different sizes and using Apple's Acoustic Seal Test in Settings. Foam tips, though more comfortable, require frequent replacement. Third-party foam tips from Comply and Foam Masters cost $25–$30 per set, but compatibility with AirPods Pro 3 requires specific connectors. A proper fit enhances sound quality and noise cancellation while reducing ear fatigue.

item.title: 6G Development Hinges on Spectrum, Investment, and 5G Completion
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: The long road towards 6G: Spectrum, investment and making 5G complete
6G development requires spectrum, investment, and completing 5G rollout. Over 5 billion 6G connections are projected by 2040, with 5G and 6G coexisting until 2035–2037. Spectrum allocation and harmonized policies are critical to ensure capacity and network quality. GSMA experts emphasize that 5G’s success relied on consistent user experience and infrastructure investment, which must continue for 5G-Advanced and 6G. Spectrum constraints could limit urban capacity by 2030, while rural areas need low-band spectrum for coverage. 6G will require 200–400 MHz channels and mid-band spectrum, with 2–2.5 GHz needed per market by 2035–2040. Past spectrum auctions showed that high prices can hinder investment, so forward-thinking policies must balance revenue with long-term network growth. Harmonization and clear roadmaps are essential to deliver economies of scale, affordable devices, and equitable access. The 2030s will focus on ensuring 6G infrastructure supports AI, sensing, and multi-device interactions, with decisions now shaping future connectivity.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: Orbital Matter 3D-Prints First Rigid Beam in Space
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: Orbital Matter 3D-printed the first rigid beam in the vacuum of space
German startup Orbital Matter 3D-printed a half-meter rigid beam in space using a custom plastic resin cured by ultraviolet light, marking the first such achievement by a free-flying spacecraft. The Replicator 2 satellite, launched this summer on a SpaceX rideshare mission, carried four 3D printers designed to extrude resin coils into cylindrical beams. CEO Jakub Stojek called the feat a proof of concept for building structures in orbit, essential for future spacecraft needing larger solar arrays and heat dissipation systems. The technology could replace foldable space structures with in-orbit assembly. Two printers were used to deploy a flexible solar array, though one failed. The company aims for 100-meter booms, surpassing SpaceX’s 20-meter Starlink arrays. A 2028 mission will test a larger printer for 5 kW solar arrays, targeting 100+ kW per wing by 2030. Orbital Matter, co-founded in 2022 by Ihnatsin and Stojek, also collaborates with satellite builders on its PADS system for deploying components.

item.title: Intel Releases 14A PDK 0.9, Advances Next-Gen Chip Manufacturing
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Intel 14A moves closer to production as PDK 0.9 becomes available
Intel Foundry released PDK 0.9 for its 14A process, marking progress toward next-gen manufacturing. The PDK, based on actual silicon measurements, allows customers to develop products with greater confidence in performance and power efficiency. Intel plans to release PDK 1.0 in Q1 2027 to validate high-volume manufacturing readiness, though mass production is expected in 2028. The 14A process includes 2nd Gen RibbonFET transistors, PowerDirect power delivery, and Turbo Cells for performance optimization. Intel is collaborating with suppliers early in development to address manufacturing challenges and improve equipment capabilities. The company is expanding its design ecosystem with partners like Cadence, Keysight, and Siemens. While customer feedback is positive, no manufacturing commitments have been disclosed. Intel emphasizes the need for external customers to recoup development costs, as current sales volumes are insufficient. The company aims to improve 14A's performance, yields, and cycle times, with future enhancements planned for 14A-E and 14A-P nodes. 'Our next major milestone is the Intel 14A PDK 1.0, expected in the first quarter of 2027,' said Ali Farhang.

item.title: Apple lets developers use Siri AI for advanced app controls
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple opens Siri AI to all developers, allowing more advanced third-party app controls
Apple's latest beta software enables third-party developers to use Siri AI for advanced app controls. The update introduces the App Intents framework, allowing developers to create custom actions and integrate Siri's understanding of context and natural language. A feature called 'skills' lets developers combine multiple actions into a single request, such as sharing product details via Messages. Siri now accesses Spotlight's semantic index to find app content beyond predefined categories. The iOS 27.3 beta demonstrates these capabilities, including organizing Safari tabs and archiving files. Apple notes these integrations are currently limited to developer testing, with customer access expected soon and App Store submissions planned for spring 2027. Google's Gemini AI assistant also offers similar developer integration through its Connected Apps Platform and Android AppFunctions.

item.title: ShotCode Offers AI-Driven Creative Direction for Video Ads
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: ShotCode bets on human creativity as AI reshapes advertising video production
ShotCode launches an AI-powered advertising studio offering creative direction for brands. The company develops video ad concepts, scripts, and finished short-form ads for SaaS companies, ecommerce brands, and consumer brands. It positions itself between self-service AI tools and traditional production, handling creative strategy while customers provide product and audience details. Industry research shows 86% of video ad buyers are using or planning to use generative AI, with 40% of ads projected to be AI-generated by 2026. Existing tools like HeyGen and Higgsfield lower production costs but leave creative decisions unresolved. ShotCode argues that AI-generated scenes may lack persuasive messaging, requiring human judgment. Freelance platforms report rising demand for AI video creators, with Upwork noting 329% year-on-year growth in AI video generation jobs. ShotCode’s model depends on brands valuing creative input over mere footage generation, as customers may eventually manage production themselves. The company aims to streamline ad creation without replacing traditional shoots, relying on its ability to deliver effective, attention-grabbing content.

item.title: Argo Space bets on water as universal propellant for space missions
item.description:
Source: Ars Technica Original headline: This space company is betting its future on a propellant available everywhere
Robert, Ryan, and Kirby Carlisle, former SpaceX engineers, founded Argo Space in late 2022 to build space infrastructure. Instead of rockets, they focused on spacecraft using water as a propellant, coolant, and radiation shield. Water, harvestable on the Moon and throughout the solar system, would enable affordable logistics like satellite resupply and refueling. Robert Carlisle emphasized water as the company’s foundation, noting it would allow spacecraft to carry more propellant and perform more tasks. Argo’s first mission, Navigator, launched in July 2022 on a Falcon 9 rideshare. While contact was established, a failed solar array deployment left the spacecraft power-negative, preventing propulsion system testing. The incident highlights challenges in testing water-based propulsion systems in space.

item.title: Nexus Mods requires AI disclosure for new mod uploads
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
Nexus Mods, the largest PC gaming mod repository, requires mod authors to disclose AI use in new uploads. Site owner Victor Folmann announced mandatory declarations about AI involvement, with tags for AI-generated and AI-assisted mods. Authors must provide public explanations of AI use in such mods. While Nexus Mods supports human creativity, it will not ban AI-generated content, citing the difficulty of distinguishing acceptable AI use. The platform will not use mods for AI training or sell them to third parties. Changes include clearer controls over mod reuse, stronger attribution rules, and adjustments to the Recently Added section to limit rapid uploads. AI-generated content will have new visibility controls. Mod authors have 60 days to update existing mods to meet requirements, with enforcement starting January 2nd.

item.title: French Engineer Builds FPGA Game Boy Console with Cartridge Ripping
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: Engineer creates retro FPGA Game Boy console that can rip your cartridges to an SD card natively
French electronics engineer Thomas Sanfourche developed the SGBC, an FPGA-based Game Boy console that plays cartridges natively and copies ROMs to microSD cards. The console replicates Game Boy hardware using an FPGA, including CPU and other components, though specific ICs aren’t detailed. It features 1080p 16:9 output with integer scaling, an SNES controller port, and a Game Boy Link port for multiplayer. Sanfourche nearly abandoned the project after professors dismissed it, but a retro gaming seller encouraged him to market it, offering financial support. The SGBC joins other FPGA retro consoles like Taki Udon’s SuperStation One and Analogue’s SuperNT+. It aims to preserve Game Boy games while adding modern features like digital archiving.

item.title: Valve updates Steam rules to cut backlog from AI game surge
item.description:
Source: Engadget, The Verge, Digital Trends Original headline: Valve Adjusts Steam Release Rules to Address Backlog Amid AI Game Surge
Valve updated Steam release rules to address a backlog caused by a surge in AI-assisted game submissions. The changes aim to reduce re-reviews and shorten approval times, which have stretched to 12 business days from the usual 3-5 days. Developers report missing launch dates by weeks, with some losing momentum and facing player complaints. New requirements mandate five minutes of Steam testing before submission, confirmation of redistributables like DirectX, and proper categorization of screenshots. Valve attributes the backlog to increased submissions, particularly from AI-generated content, which often requires minimal pre-release checks. An analysis shows 49.9% of October 2026 Steam games disclosed AI use, up from 1.7% in January 2024. Developers like structmira and 2 Left Thumbs highlight the impact of delays, with structmira noting backlash over a late release despite a successful trailer. Valve says further improvements are planned but emphasizes the need to balance innovation with quality control as AI integration grows.

item.title: China Outlines Moon Crew Landing Plan by 2030
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: China Details Its Plan to Land Astronauts on the Moon Before 2030
China outlined its plan to land astronauts on the Moon by 2030, detailing a series of missions during the 7th Manned Space Symposium. Chief designer Wang Xiang described steps including a lunar orbit rendezvous, uncrewed lander tests, and a 2029 rehearsal mission. The program will use Long March 10A and 10 rockets to test systems, with a crewed landing targeting 2030. Three taikonauts, two of whom will land, are planned for a three-day surface mission. The timeline shifts from previous vague goals, with preparations underway at Wenchang spaceport. NASA aims for a 2028 Artemis 4 landing, but uncertainty remains over commercial partner readiness. China’s approach mirrors Apollo-era orbital docking methods, setting the stage for a lunar race with the U.S.

item.title: iPhone Duo Gets Reachability for Easier One-Handed Use
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: iPhone Duo’s huge display just got a little easier to navigate with iOS 27.3
Apple adds Reachability to iPhone Duo in iOS 27.3 beta, enabling one-handed use with swipe gestures. The feature allows users to shift content between sides of the foldable screen by swiping left or right from edges. It is enabled via Settings > Accessibility > Reachability and activates by default upon software update. iOS 27.3 also expands Siri’s capabilities across apps like Music, Messages, Photos, Calendar, and Reminders. Users can now request Siri to build playlists, schedule texts, edit photos, create calendar events, organize Safari tabs, and manage files. New features also appear in Weather, Maps, Preview, and Shortcuts. Third-party developers will gain access to these tools. The update remains in developer beta testing with a public release planned later this year.

item.title: Canva to Lay Off 22% of Staff Amid Restructuring
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Canva is announcing changes and layoffs affecting 22 percent of its staff
Canva is laying off 22 percent of its staff, affecting 1,271 employees, according to CEO Melanie Perkins. The restructuring includes role changes, relocations to centralized hubs, and layoffs. Perkins stated that the company needs to refocus on its roots of small, empowered teams. Changes involve merging Product, Growth, and Platform teams into one organization, consolidating responsibilities, and making Sydney the primary location for product teams and roles requiring close collaboration. Starting in January, most hybrid employees will be expected to work 2 to 3 days in the office weekly. Severance packages include at least six months of salary, twelve months of healthcare coverage, and career support. Squarespace also announced similar layoffs affecting 19 percent of its staff.

item.title: Samsung's Sleep Apnea Detection Now FDA-Cleared for Galaxy Ring and Watch 9
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Samsung upgraded its Sleep Apnea detection—Galaxy Ring, Watch 9 are receiving it now
Samsung's upgraded Sleep Apnea detection software has received FDA clearance in the U.S. and MFDS approval in South Korea for the Galaxy Ring and Watch 9. The feature is now rolling out in the Health app, offering deeper insights into breathing disruptions for users to share with doctors. Samsung claims it is the first company to bring sleep apnea risk detection to a smart ring, with the upgraded version providing more detailed data on nighttime breathing patterns. Users need two nights of monitoring within a 10-day period to see insights. The Galaxy Watch 9 and Ring are available now with Wear OS 7 or higher, while older Galaxy Watch 7 and 8 models require a pending software update. Samsung first announced the feature at Galaxy Unpacked in 2024, with U.S. approval finalized in 2024 and South Korea's in 2023. The company emphasizes the importance of early detection for sleep apnea, a condition that can cause serious health issues if untreated.

item.title: EloElo raises $80M from NBCUniversal for India's microdrama market
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: India’s EloElo nabs $80M from NBCUniversal to bet on the country’s rising microdrama market
EloElo raised $80 million in Series C funding from Hornbill Capital and NBCUniversal, boosting its total fundraising to $130 million and valuation to $500 million. The investment targets India’s growing microdrama market, where over 118 million users watch serialized content monthly. EloElo’s Story TV app, with 33 million active users, competes with platforms like YouTube and TikTok. Founder Saurabh Pandey emphasized mobile-first content consumption, noting users spend 95 minutes daily on the app. He argued that serialized storytelling requires AI tools to enhance production, with EloElo’s Dolphin AI platform now available to creators. Despite challenges in monetizing free content, the company offers subscriptions and ads. Analysts predict the microdrama industry could reach $3-$4 billion annually by 2030. EloElo also operates a vertical video learning app and AI companion tool, with over 40 million monthly users across platforms. The round included investments from MIT Investment Co. and existing backers.

item.title: US Army Flies Hybrid Drone with 3D-Printed Engine and 400V System
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: US Army successfully flies a hybrid electric drone with 3D-printed heavy-fuel rotary engine — 400v motor-generator uses advanced engineering to ditch a bulky liquid cooling system
The U.S. Army successfully flew the VICTOR hybrid electric drone, which uses a 3D-printed heavy-fuel rotary engine designed to run on JP8 fuel. JP8, a denser kerosene-based fuel with a flash point of 140℉, is less volatile than gasoline and harder to atomize, requiring higher compression and posing challenges for efficiency. Researchers at the Army Research Laboratory used computational fluid dynamics and a clean-sheet design approach to optimize the engine, leveraging 3D metal printing to create an air-cooled system that eliminated the need for a bulky liquid cooling system. Dr. Kweon noted that rapid iteration allowed improvements in fuel atomization and reduced compression leaks. The engine powers a 400-volt motor-generator instead of directly driving propellers, similar to hybrid EVs, enabling independent optimal RPM operation. The VTOL drone can take off and land without a runway, with a battery system allowing flight without the engine. The Army has not disclosed details about the drone’s battery configuration.

item.title: Microsoft Enhances Windows 11 Performance for 8GB RAM Systems
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, PCWorld, Latest from Tom's Hardware
Microsoft released updates for Windows 11 26H2 to improve performance on 8GB RAM systems. The updates, included in build 26300.9818 or later, enhance multitasking speed by up to 40% and responsiveness by 20% through memory management refinements. These changes keep up to 2GB more active data in RAM, reducing app reload times. Memory savings across Windows, Edge, and 365 apps can cut committed-memory growth by up to 900MB, with Word, Excel, and Outlook saving up to 360MB. Edge launches 33% faster, and Teams Efficiency Mode reduces launch times by 20%. Microsoft also employs smarter compression techniques to expand 8GB RAM capacity by up to 2GB. The updates aim to make 8GB systems viable for everyday tasks despite RAM shortages and rising costs. PCWorld notes other software developers have not yet optimized for 8GB, while Intel warns of prolonged memory shortages. Microsoft plans further refinements with PC makers and silicon providers to balance affordability and performance.
item.source: Digital Trends, PCWorld, Latest from Tom's Hardware

item.title: Google's AI Policy Forces Schools to Choose Between Tools and Search Access
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, Ars Technica, TechCrunch, Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google's AI Policy Shift Forces Schools to Choose Between AI Tools and Search Access
Google will disable AI tools like Gemini and Google Search by default for K-12 student accounts starting early 2027. Schools can manually enable individual AI services, but blocking all AI features will revoke Google Search access. Google’s vice president for education, Chris Phillips, told The New York Times that 'Search and AI are deeply integrated,' meaning schools opting out of AI will lose Search access. Critics, including former FTC chair Lina Khan, argue the policy forces schools into an 'AI-or-nothing' dilemma, leveraging Google’s search dominance to push AI adoption. The policy follows consultations with educators and policymakers to address concerns about AI chatbots enabling cheating and misinformation. Schools enabling AI will gain access to 'Guided Learning' tools for step-by-step problem-solving. Critics say the requirement to disable AI entirely to retain Search access undermines educational choice, while Google claims the change offers greater control. The decision highlights Google’s influence in education, where its services like Chromebooks and Classroom are widely used.
item.source: Digital Trends, Ars Technica, TechCrunch, Latest from Android Central

item.title: AI inference startup Fal doubles valuation to $16B on rising demand
item.description:
Source: TechCrunch Original headline: AI inference startup Fal doubles its valuation to $16B as demand surges
Fal, a San Francisco-based AI inference startup, raised $1.3 billion in its latest funding round, doubling its valuation to $16 billion from $8 billion in April. The Series F round, led by Bessemer Venture Partners with participation from Nvidia and T. Rowe Price, marks a combined $1.65 billion raised across Series E and F rounds. The funding comes as demand for inference services surges, driven by customers using open-source models. Fal surpassed $800 million in annualized revenue this year. Other inference service providers like Baseten and Fireworks AI also report rapid growth but face thin gross margins due to high compute costs. Fal was co-founded in 2021 by Burkay Gur, a former Coinbase machine learning leader, and Gorkem Yurtseven, a former Amazon developer.

item.title: Meta Ends Feature Development for Quest 2 and Quest Pro
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Meta's Quest 2 and Quest Pro reach 'end of feature development'
Meta announced the end of feature development for Quest 2 and Quest Pro headsets. Final operating system updates will arrive in March 2027, with security patches and bugfixes continuing through December 2027. Developers will have until December 2027 to submit new apps for these devices, though existing apps can still receive updates. Users will retain access to app stores and cross-play functionality with Quest 3 and Quest 3S devices. The company noted millions of users continue to use the Quest 2 and Quest Pro despite their 2020 and 2022 release dates. Meta is shifting focus to newer products like its VR Glasses lineup, signaling a strategic pivot toward future wearables.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old AirPods Can Be Repurposed or Repaired, Apple Says
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't throw away your old AirPods — do this instead
Apple advises against discarding old AirPods, suggesting battery replacements or repurposing. Battery replacement costs $49 per earbud ($98 for both) versus $249 for new AirPods Pro. AppleCare users may get free replacements if battery capacity drops below 80%. Independent repairs are possible but risk voiding warranties. Replacement prices vary: $89 for a Pro earbud, $69 for a standard one. Recycling is free via Apple's program with prepaid shipping labels. Alternatives include selling through buyback services, gifting, or using as backup earbuds. Old AirPods can serve as gym earbuds, sleep headphones, or Roku audio devices. Proper disposal is encouraged to avoid lithium-ion battery hazards.

item.title: Arkane Studios May Move to Ubisoft as Xbox Weighs Sale Options
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Arkane and its Blade game may end up at Ubisoft as Xbox considers offers
Arkane Studios may leave Microsoft as Xbox explores selling the developer. Reports indicate multiple companies, including Ubisoft and at least two unnamed firms, have made bids for the studio. Xbox has considered offers ahead of a December deadline but has not confirmed details. The studio's Blade game adaptation, based on Marvel's character, remains in development despite earlier layoffs at Xbox in July. Arkane, known for titles like Dishonored and Deathloop, could continue the project under a new owner. Ubisoft, however, faces its own industry challenges, having announced layoffs in January, March, June, and October. A representative from Xbox declined to elaborate on the situation, leaving the studio's future uncertain but with potential for a new ownership arrangement.

item.title: Reddit Tests Search Ads Amid Declining Traffic and Revenue Concerns
item.description:
Source: Engadget, TechCrunch
Reddit is testing search ads to address declining traffic and revenue challenges. The platform will show ads based on search queries, such as linking 'espresso station' to coffee products or 'home office setup' to office equipment. The test involves limited advertisers and aims to refine ad placement before wider rollout. Ads will appear near the top of search results, though frequency is unspecified. CEO Steve Huffman noted Reddit is the only platform without a 'logged-in only' model, which improves ad targeting by restricting access to authenticated users. The move follows a 2% year-over-year drop in U.S. daily active users to 50.7 million, with global users flat at 130.3 million. Reddit warned of potential further declines if trends persist. The company’s stock fell after forecasting fourth-quarter sales between $1 billion and $1.03 billion, below analyst expectations. The logged-in only model aims to prevent AI scraping and enhance advertiser data, following restrictions on developer access and Old Reddit. The ad test coincides with reduced referral traffic from Google’s AI-powered search features, which provide answers directly on search pages.

item.title: Casio Launches New Ring-Sized Watch Based on 1995 Design
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Another Ring-Sized Casio Watch Has Hit the Market
Casio has released the CRW-002, a ring-sized watch based on its 1995 A168 model. The device offers basic functions like timekeeping, a 1/100-second stopwatch, water resistance, and adjustable backlight timing. It features an injection-molded metal casing with three side buttons and a six-digit LCD screen, powered by a compact module. The ring fits a size 10.5 finger (size 22 in Japan) with spacers for smaller sizes. It is available in silver ($135) and gold ($155) finishes, launching in November. Casio positions the CRW-002 as a simpler alternative to smart rings, emphasizing its minimalistic design and lack of complex features. The watch is part of the company’s effort to reinterpret classic designs into wearable form factors, following earlier ring versions inspired by its G-Shock line and health-tracking models like the CRW-H001. The CRW-002’s limited adjustability and basic functionality contrast with its predecessors, offering a streamlined experience.

item.title: PC Makers Shift Production Back to China Amid Rising Costs
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: Major PC makers are shifting production back to China as costs rise — HP, Asus among firms moving work in efficiency push
HP and Asus are shifting PC production from Thailand and Vietnam back to China due to rising AI-driven component costs, which are squeezing hardware margins. TrendForce projects the share of notebooks built outside China will drop from 24% in 2025 to 21% in 2026, with no immediate price relief. Chinese assemblers like Luxshare and Huaqin are winning contracts by offering cheaper memory access and waiving engineering fees, while traditional Taiwanese ODMs like Quanta focus on higher-margin AI servers. A chip industry executive noted cost pressures extend beyond memory, with memory and storage now accounting for 40% of a PC’s price. PC makers are prioritizing cost efficiency over diversification, as global PC shipments fell 20.1% year-over-year in Q3 2026. Acer’s CEO expects prices to rise 5-20% in Q4 2026, while SK hynix warns demand will outstrip supply until 2030. The shift reverses the China+1 strategy, with China reclaiming manufacturing share as the cheapest option amid supply chain realignments.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: iOS 27.3 Adds New StandBy Faces, Customization
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Your iPhone’s StandBy mode is getting new clocks, Calendar, and Weather faces with iOS 27.3
Apple’s iOS 27.3 update introduces new StandBy features for iPhones supporting the feature. The update includes refreshed clocks with expanded color options and additional complications, plus new Calendar and Weather faces. Photos now display Shared Albums. Users can customize multiple versions of each face and switch between them. The iPhone Duo retains exclusive StandBy functionality when folded or propped open without charging. Other models require a charger and sideways position. The update, available in a developer beta, is expected for public release in December. StandBy remains a limited feature, accessible only to compatible devices.

item.title: Nintendo Releases Ocarina of Time Remake for Switch 2 on November 5
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: All the news about The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake
Nintendo is releasing a Switch 2 remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time on November 5, 28 years after its original 1998 launch. The remake features enhanced visuals, modern controls like a dedicated jump button and sprint, full voice acting, and a 'Threads of Time' progress tracker. Developers emphasized preserving the original experience while improving accessibility for modern players. A special Switch 2 console and Pro Controller with Triforce designs are also launching. The remake, described as a 'faithful interpretation using modern technologies,' will be the first Zelda title exclusive to the Switch 2. Preorders offer a $10 discount, with physical copies priced at $59.99 before a potential $10 increase. The release coincides with Grand Theft Auto VI's launch. Nintendo's art director noted the remake's visual style draws inspiration from puppet shows and practical effects, aiming to evoke nostalgia while creating a convincing fantasy world.

item.title: Apple Revamps Health App, Adds Gym Strength Plans in iOS 27.3 Beta
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: Apple’s redesigned Health app returns in iOS 27.3 beta, alongside personalized Fitness+ gym plans
Apple’s redesigned Health app has returned in the iOS 27.3 beta after being removed from the previous 27.2 beta. The update introduces Apple Intelligence-powered features, including Health Age to assess health relative to age, movement assessments, and dynamic data visualization. Expanded language support now includes French, Japanese, Korean, Spanish, Portuguese, and others. The Health app also offers personalized wellness recommendations based on device-collected data. Meanwhile, Apple Fitness+ gains Gym Strength, a feature creating four-week strength training plans tailored to user experience, fitness goals, schedule, and gym equipment. Users can customize workout days, muscle focus, session duration, and receive exercise specifics with video demos. Plans adapt based on training consistency and progress, available on iPhone, iPad, and Apple Watch for logging metrics. The updates aim to simplify gym routines and enhance health tracking.

item.title: Smugglers bypass export rules to smuggle HBM chips from South Korea to China
item.description:
Source: Latest from Tom's Hardware Original headline: AI chip smugglers exploit trade control loophole to bring banned HBM from South Korea into China
Smugglers bypass export controls by pairing low-performance processors with banned HBM chips from South Korea, allowing the memory components to enter China undetected. The smuggler’s firm produces cheap, export-controlled processors that are then combined with high-end HBM from Samsung and SK hynix. These hybrid chips are smuggled via Hong Kong, where technicians extract the HBM chips, which are then sold to Chinese AI labs at inflated prices. A Shenzhen broker reports HBM3E prices rose from hundreds to $4,000, with each AI GPU requiring six to eight chips, generating $24,000 to $32,000 in profit. Chinese firms like Huawei face shortages, with its Ascend 950DT priced at $37,000 despite lower performance than Nvidia’s B200. Huawei’s next-gen 960DT aims to match H100 performance but relies on external HBM sources. Smugglers warn of impending crackdowns by South Korea and the U.S., citing recent arrests of tech executives and increased anti-smuggling efforts in Taiwan and Malaysia.

item.title: Xiaomi Rolls Out HyperOS 4 to 80+ Devices in 2026 Update
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: HyperOS 4 update schedule: Every Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO phone getting Android 17
Xiaomi will roll out HyperOS 4 to over 80 devices across its Xiaomi, Redmi, and POCO brands in 2026. The update, based on Android 17, is divided into three waves starting November 2026. The first wave includes Xiaomi 17 and 15 series, Redmi Note 17 and 15 families, POCO F8 and X8 lineups, and Xiaomi Pad 8 tablets. The second wave begins mid-November with Xiaomi 15T series, POCO F7 and F9 families, Xiaomi Pad 7, and other tablets. The final wave in December covers Xiaomi 14 and 13 series, Xiaomi MIX Flip, Redmi Note 14 family, and POCO F6 series. HyperOS 4 features a "Soft Light Glass" UI with translucent panels, redesigned notifications, and customizable lock screens. Performance improvements include faster app launches and reduced HDR photo capture times. The update also introduces Super XiaoAi 2.0, an AI assistant with enhanced task capabilities. Privacy features like confirmation prompts for data actions and expanded Super Island support are included. Some features remain limited to China-specific versions. The rollout highlights Xiaomi's focus on global AI integration and UI innovation.

item.title: Apple Enforces Stricter Age Limits on Dating and AI Apps
item.description:
Source: PCMag, TechCrunch, Gizmodo Original headline: Apple Tightens App Store Age Restrictions for Dating and AI Companion Apps
Apple is enforcing stricter age restrictions on dating and AI companion apps, requiring developers to label apps with features enabling sexual or romantic interactions by November 16. These apps will receive an 18+ rating, limiting minors' access. Location-sharing features must also be disclosed, raising privacy concerns in regions like Brazil, where such apps require a 16+ rating. Apps including Bumble, Tinder, Replika, and Nomi AI are affected. The U.S. lacks similar legislation, though location-sharing may not be clearly labeled. AI chatbots like Character.AI and xAI’s 3D companions, which have over 220 million downloads, face new rules. OpenAI delayed its adult mode for ChatGPT. Experts warn of mental health risks from AI interactions, citing cases like a retiree who died after responding to a fake AI invitation. Developers must comply by January 12, 2027. Apple’s changes aim to enhance child safety through parental controls and age ratings, though effectiveness remains under scrutiny as AI and dating apps evolve.

item.title: LG TVs to Enable Food Ordering via AI Partnership
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: LG smart TVs will soon be the new place where you can order food
SoundHound AI and LG Electronics are launching a service allowing users to order food directly from LG Smart TVs starting in December. The feature will be available on approximately 20 million TVs in the US, enabling customers to browse menus, select items, and complete payments through the TV interface. A picture-in-picture view will let users continue watching content while ordering. For restaurants, the system integrates with existing point-of-sale and kitchen systems, eliminating the need for new hardware. Transaction routing and secure checkout are handled by the platform. The first participating restaurant brands are expected to be announced late 2026. SoundHound already powers AI food orders for chains like Jersey Mike’s, Five Guys, and White Castle, which operate over 15,000 locations. The partnership aims to expand to retail and other merchant categories in the future.

item.title: Front USB Ports May Slow Connected Devices
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Your desktop's front USB ports may be slowing down every device you plug into them
Front USB ports on desktops may slow connected devices due to design limitations. These ports use extension cables to reach I/O controllers, causing signal loss and reduced speed compared to rear ports, which are soldered directly to the motherboard. Front ports often share a single connector, splitting power and bandwidth among multiple devices. For example, the ASUS ROG Maximus Z790 Hero motherboard offers high-speed rear ports but limits front ports to shared 5 Gbps speeds. Macs also have slower front USB-C ports compared to rear Thunderbolt 4 ports. High-speed peripherals like external SSDs or VR headsets should use rear ports for optimal performance, while low-power devices like mice or keyboards work fine on front ports. Users should check motherboard specs to identify port speeds and allocate devices accordingly.

item.title: macOS 27.3 Beta Adds Markdown Preview in Quick Look
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: You can finally preview Markdown files in Quick Look on your Mac
macOS 27.3 beta adds Markdown preview support in Quick Look. The update includes Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and Siri AI enhancements. Quick Look now renders Markdown files with proper formatting, allowing users to preview structured text without opening external apps. Markdown, a plain-text formatting language introduced in 2004 by John Gruber, is widely used for documentation and AI agent instructions. Apple integrates Markdown across its ecosystem, with Notes supporting import/export and Siri AI using SKILL.md files for app task handling. The change simplifies workflow for users who rely on Markdown, enabling quick formatting checks directly in Quick Look.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Ubuntu 26.04 Changes Improve Performance on Older PCs
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: 5 Ubuntu 26.04 changes that breathe new life into an old PC
Ubuntu 26.04 recommends 6GB RAM for smoother performance on older PCs. Five changes can improve system responsiveness without hardware upgrades. Memory compression via Zswap reduces disk activity by storing compressed pages in RAM. Zswap can be enabled with terminal commands, though settings reset on reboot. Swappiness adjustments and distinction between Zswap/Zram are noted. Switching to lightweight desktops like LXQt frees up RAM, increasing available memory by 0.4GiB in tests. Disabling background apps and autostart entries reduces resource usage, with some apps overlooked during testing. Reviewing GNOME extensions and disabling unused ones cuts background activity. Reduced Motion setting minimizes animations for faster navigation, though it doesn't directly free RAM. These tweaks offer modest improvements, with LXQt and background app management showing clearest gains. Users can try these methods before upgrading hardware.

item.title: Sonos Launches New Presets and AI Voice Assistant Beta
item.description:
Source: The Verge Original headline: Sonos adds new Presets and prepares for the 27voice AI beta
Sonos is releasing an app update featuring new Presets for quick music playback in specific rooms and early access to its AI voice assistant. Users can create Presets to set volume and room-specific playback, appearing on the homescreen. Early access to the Sonos 27voice AI assistant is available via a waitlist opening November 6th, with access starting November 12th. The AI can handle complex tasks like playing albums based on cover art or answering trivia questions followed by music playback. These updates aim to recover from a 2024 app redesign criticized by CEO Tom Conrad, with a revamped app OS launched in September. Additional features include swipe navigation for skipping tracks, rearranging favorites, and integration with iOS System Health for setup diagnostics.

item.title: Safari Gets Vertical Tabs, Dark Mode, and Siri in iOS 27.3 Update
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends, Gizmodo Original headline: Safari Gains Vertical Tabs, Adaptive Dark Mode, and Siri Integration in Upcoming iOS 27.3 Update
Apple’s Safari browser will get vertical tabs, adaptive dark mode, and Siri integration in the upcoming iOS 27.3 update. Vertical tabs, appearing as a left-hand sidebar with favicon icons, will let users organize tabs into groups on iPad and iPhone Duo devices but not standard iPhones. Adaptive dark mode dynamically adjusts website visuals, darkening backgrounds and enhancing contrast, but is limited to macOS. Siri integration allows voice commands to manage tabs, such as sorting or closing them, requiring Apple Intelligence-capable devices. The updates, available in developer betas, are expected in December. Gizmodo noted Siri can now understand entire websites without scrolling. Audio Intelligence features for Apple Watch are also in the beta but unrelated to Safari. These changes aim to improve tab management and visual customization.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Old laptop SSDs can be repurposed as external storage
item.description:
Source: Engadget Original headline: Don't throw away your laptop's old SSDs — do this instead
Old laptop SSDs can be repurposed as external storage. Removing the SSD from an unused laptop may be possible, though some models like Apple's MacBooks solder storage to the logic board. If removable, pairing it with an external enclosure allows conversion into high-speed external storage. Affordable enclosures are available for 2.5-inch SATA or M.2 NVMe SSDs. Before repurposing, check for important files and SSD health using macOS Disk Utility or Windows Drive Management. If the SSD is nearing the end of its life, only store non-critical data. Format the SSD to wipe data and install it in the enclosure, which connects via USB-C for use as an external drive. This reduces e-waste and extends SSD lifespan.

item.title: Google dismantles Android TV botnet but warns infected devices remain risky
item.description:
Source: Latest from Android Central Original headline: Google takes down a massive Android TV botnet, but infected devices remain dangerous
Google dismantled a large Android TV botnet operated by Videostrong Technology, which embedded malware called XCPE into firmware of 1.3 million devices. The malware, used for generating fake ad views, rerouting traffic, and installing additional malware, grants attackers system-level privileges to install apps, take screenshots, and collect data. XCPE persists by restoring from a protected firmware partition and can bypass Google Play Protect. Users must replace infected devices rather than relying on app uninstallation. Google banned Videostrong from certified Android device production and collaborated with law enforcement and security firms to disable command servers, potentially removing 10 million more compromised devices. The company enhanced firmware checks and manufacturer vetting after discovering Videostrong used obfuscation to load malicious code post-boot.

item.title: The Elder Scrolls VI Reveals Title as 'Sentinel'
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: After a Decade, ‘The Elder Scrolls VI’ Finally Has … a Name
Bethesda announced the title of The Elder Scrolls VI during its 40th-anniversary video, narrated by Todd Howard. The game, set in the region of Hammerfell, is named 'The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel.' The reveal included an epigraph from Yazar, the Moth Priest of High Queen Iradne of Hammerfell, which reads: 'The scroll offered only a shimmer, a veil thinly lifted to my eyes. A future lost. A victory undone. Sands of time scattered by fate.' No release date or gameplay details were provided, though the name was revealed after over a decade of development. The announcement focused on the title, with no additional information about the game's content or timeline.

item.title: YouTube Explores Tamba as Potential Social Network
item.description:
Source: Digital Trends Original headline: YouTube might get its own social network since Shorts obviously wasn’t addictive enough
YouTube is testing a new social platform called Tamba, according to findings by Android Authority. The project, discovered in version 21.44.534 of the YouTube app, includes a sandbox app package named com.google.android.youtube.sandbox. Tamba features a distinct design with custom icons for home, search, camera, inbox, chat, and content creation. Code references suggest functionalities like followers, follow requests, direct messaging, group chats, and photo/video sharing. Some strings indicate Shorts videos could be played within conversations, blending YouTube’s video library with social features. The app’s experimental nature is highlighted by terms like 'sandbox' and labeled icons. While YouTube recently added direct messaging, Tamba could expand into private profiles and social feeds. However, no official launch details or timeline have been confirmed.

item.title: INSTRUCTION: Maker creates Bluetooth tracker using ESP32 and nRF Connect app
item.description:
Source: How-To Geek Original headline: I built a weekend Bluetooth tracker from an ESP32, and nRF Connect does the rest
A maker created a Bluetooth tracker using an ESP32 board and nRF Connect app. The project involved programming the ESP32 with open-source firmware via Arduino IDE, then using the app to monitor signal strength. The tracker detected range changes, showing signal strength dropping to -90 dBm at 40 feet. While it mimics AirTag-like functionality for proximity alerts, it lacks network-based tracking capabilities. The maker noted the device could serve as a basic 'left behind' alert tool with added batteries. The project highlights ESP32's versatility for weekend maker tasks, despite setup challenges like syntax errors and Linux group permissions. The tracker's range matches standard AirTags, but its limited tracking features position it as a learning project rather than a practical replacement for commercial trackers.

item.title: Revolut slashes AI costs by replacing Claude with self-hosted Chinese models
item.description:
Source: Latest from TechRadar US in News Original headline: 'We were highly skeptical about the cost of AI': Revolut reveals it cut AI coding costs by cutting out Claude entirely
Revolut replaced Anthropic's Claude with self-hosted Z.ai models, cutting AI inference costs by 90% and improving productivity. The bank's Infrastructure Lead, David Abitbol, cited skepticism about AI costs, noting strict budget limits during initial deployment. Self-hosted models from Z.ai, running on 56 Nvidia B200 GPUs with 380GB+ memory, offer data privacy and auditability. Productivity metrics show 70% faster lead times and 60% reduced coding time. While self-hosting eliminates token cost unpredictability, it requires significant hardware investment. Abitbol emphasized flat billing and cost predictability, stating open-source models are now a priority. Despite cost savings, deploying AI remains expensive, with self-hosting offering potential long-term economic benefits over commercial models.
item.source: Latest from TechRadar US in News

item.title: El Niño Drives Record Rainfall Across U.S. as Winter Looms
item.description:
Source: Gizmodo Original headline: Winter Hasn’t Even Started, and El Niño Is Already Drenching the US From Coast to Coast
Extreme rainfall has struck multiple U.S. regions, with Florida recording up to 2 feet of rain and flash flooding killing two in Palm Bay. The National Weather Service warns Southeast Florida may see more rain for at least another day. Southwest states like Arizona faced up to 7 inches of rain, causing evacuations and two deaths, including one in a drainage tunnel. A storm system now affects the Central U.S., with potential impacts on midterm voter turnout. An atmospheric river is expected to bring heavy rain to the West Coast from November 10-12. Meteorologist Ben Noll notes recent rainfall is likely the start of a harsh winter. El Niño, the strongest on record, is driving these storms by shifting weather patterns and increasing atmospheric moisture. Global warming exacerbates the effect, contributing to record heat and humidity in August 2026. NOAA’s winter outlook predicts wetter-than-average conditions from the Southwest to the Southeast and East Coast. The events highlight long-term climate risks as fossil fuel pollution intensifies extreme rainfall threats.
